conventions.convention: Computational reproducibility holds input data, computational steps, methods and code, and analysis conditions fixed. Input data follow the stated curation steps; relevant conditions include the computational environment.

Replicability requires consistent results across studies addressing the same scientific question using newly obtained study-specific data. New data establish only a replication attempt; probabilistic independence and different investigators are not required.
Transparent reporting records relevant artifacts, restrictions, methods, decisions, computational conditions, uncertainty and limitations; it guarantees neither correctness nor future replication.

Group means are unweighted arithmetic means of nonempty groups; empty-group means are undefined. The contrast is older minus younger, with younger defined by age at most the cut point. All synthetic rows are retained, and no uncertainty model or consistency threshold is assumed.

load_bearing.statement: Computational reproducibility means consistent results with the same input data, computational steps, methods and code, and analysis conditions. Replicability means consistent results across studies answering the same scientific question, each using newly obtained data; consistency requires accounting for relevant uncertainty and material method differences.
